metadata.name: World Federation of Neurosurgical Societies (WFNS) scale
metadata.summary: 5-grade aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage scale combining GCS and presence of motor deficit.
clinical_pearls: Reassess WFNS grade after resuscitation or EVD placement for acute hydrocephalus.
Combines objective Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) strata with presence of major focal motor deficit, yielding better interobserver reliability than the Hunt and Hess scale (Degen et al., 2011).
Pitfall — Hydrocephalus & sedation confounding: Pre-resuscitation WFNS grading can overestimate severity in patients with treatable acute hydrocephalus, post-ictal state, or sedating medications.
Pitfall — Wide GCS 7–12 Grade IV band: Grade IV spans a broad consciousness range (GCS 7–12) with heterogeneous outcomes, motivating modified WFNS proposals (Rosen & Macdonald, 2004).

references.citation: Teasdale GM, Drake CG, Hunt W, et al. A universal subarachnoid hemorrhage scale: report of a committee of the World Federation of Neurosurgical Societies. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry. 1988;51(11):1457.

Rosen DS, Macdonald RL. Grading of subarachnoid hemorrhage: modification of the World Federation of Neurosurgical Societies scale on the basis of data for a large series of patients. Neurosurgery. 2004;54(3):566-575.
Degen LA, Dorhout Mees SM, Algra A, Rinkel GJ. Interobserver variability of grading scales for aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage. Stroke. 2011;42(6):1546-1549.

interpretation.label: Good-Grade SAH (WFNS I–II)
interpretation.summary: Good baseline neurological grade; favorable prognosis with prompt aneurysm securing.

interpretation.label: Poor-Grade SAH (WFNS IV–V)
interpretation.summary: Poor baseline grade; evaluate for reversible hydrocephalus/ICP and neurocritical care support.

assessment_guides.title: WFNS Grade II vs Grade III (Motor Deficit)
bedside_steps: Verify whether the patient has hemiparesis/limb motor deficit (or aphasia in some centers) with GCS 13–14.
pitfalls_and_exceptions: An isolated cranial nerve palsy (e.g., CN III palsy from PCom aneurysm) without limb motor deficit does NOT upgrade Grade II to Grade III.
